questions.topic: Atomic number, isotopes and atomic mass
questions.stem: If an atom of an element is represented as 40/20 Y, this shows that it has
questions.explanation: The lower number (20) is the atomic number, i.e. the number of protons; the mass number is 40.

questions.stem: When metals react, they usually do so by
questions.explanation: Metals are electropositive and react by losing electrons to form cations.

questions.topic: Atomic number, isotopes and atomic mass
questions.stem: If the mass number of X is 24 and X^2+ contains 10 electrons, the nucleus of X will consist of
questions.explanation: The neutral atom has 10 + 2 = 12 electrons, so 12 protons; neutrons = 24 - 12 = 12.

questions.stem: The atom and ion of chlorine have the same
questions.explanation: Forming Cl^- changes only the number of electrons; the number of protons stays 17.

questions.stem: Element X has 2 electrons in its outer shell while element Y has 6. The compound formed by X and Y has the formula
questions.explanation: X forms X^2+ and Y forms Y^2-, so they combine 1 : 1 as XY.

questions.stem: "Electrons will occupy equivalent orbitals singly, as far as possible, with the same spin" is a statement of
questions.explanation: This is Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity.

questions.topic: Acids, bases and salts as electrolytes
questions.stem: M is a group II element. Which of the following represents the ionization of its chloride?
questions.explanation: A group II metal forms M^2+, so the chloride is MCl2 which ionizes to M^2+ and two Cl^- ions.

questions.stem: Which of the following forms a coordinate covalent bond with H^+?
questions.explanation: The oxygen of water donates a lone pair to H^+ to form H3O^+.

questions.stem: How many electrons are present in the 2p orbital of an element represented as 19/9 X?
questions.explanation: Z = 9: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^5, so there are 5 electrons in the 2p sub-level.

questions.topic: Atomic number, isotopes and atomic mass
questions.stem: The emission of a beta particle from the nucleus of 226/88 Ra will produce
questions.explanation: Beta emission leaves the mass number unchanged and raises the atomic number by 1: 226/89 Ac.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents correctly the rearrangement of particles during double decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: In double decomposition the partners are exchanged, the positive parts P and R each combining with the other's negative part: PS and RQ.

questions.stem: Two corked vessels of different capacities contain 0.01 mole each of gases X and Y, maintained at the same temperature. Which of the following will be the same for X and Y?
options: Frequency of collision of their molecules
questions.explanation: Equal numbers of moles contain equal numbers of molecules (0.01 x 6.02 x 10^23).

questions.stem: A given volume of oxygen diffuses through a porous plug in 8.0 seconds. How long will it take the same volume of sulphur (IV) oxide to diffuse through under the same conditions? [O = 16; SO2 = 64]
questions.explanation: Graham's law: t is proportional to sqrt(M), so t = 8.0 x sqrt(64/32) = 11.3 s.

questions.stem: The number of hydroxonium ions produced by one molecule of an acid in aqueous solution is known as its
questions.explanation: Basicity is the number of replaceable hydrogen (H3O^+) ions per molecule of acid.

questions.stem: Consider the following equation: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2. Calculate the mass of sodium required to produce 0.40 g of sodium hydroxide. [H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23]
questions.explanation: 0.40 g NaOH = 0.40/40 = 0.010 mol, which needs 0.010 mol Na = 0.23 g.

questions.stem: In which of the following reactions is hydrogen sulphide behaving as an acid?
questions.explanation: H2S neutralises the base NH4OH to give a salt and water; in B and C it acts as a reducing agent.

questions.topic: Reactions of acids with metals, oxides and trioxocarbonates (IV)
questions.stem: Hydrogen is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
questions.explanation: Iron is above hydrogen in the activity series and displaces it from dilute HCl; ions cannot, and copper is below hydrogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties distinguishes concentrated H2SO4 from concentrated HNO3?
options: Ability to conduct electricity on dilution
Ability to liberate CO2 from CO3^2-
questions.explanation: Both acids conduct, liberate CO2 and oxidize, but only concentrated H2SO4 is a dehydrating agent.

questions.stem: Consider the general equation below: XnCO3(s) --heat--> XnO(s) + CO2(g). The reaction will not occur when X is
questions.explanation: Sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) is stable to heat; the carbonates of Cu, Mg and Zn decompose.

questions.stem: Which of the following conclusions about a solution of pH 4 is correct?
options: It contains more OH^- than H3O^+.
It is more acidic than a solution of pH 2.
Its hydrogen ion concentration is 4.0 x 10^-1 mol dm^-3.

questions.stem: An energy profile diagram for the reaction between A and B shows the energy of the reactants A + B, rising to a peak, and then falling to the products AB at an energy level lower than that of A + B. Which of the following can be deduced from the energy profile diagram? The reaction between A and B
questions.explanation: The products lie at a lower energy than the reactants, so heat is given out (delta H negative).

questions.stem: The presence of catalyst in a reaction mixture alters the
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway of lower activation energy; it does not change delta H, yield or equilibrium position.

questions.stem: Rate curves (total volume of CO2 evolved against time) represent the reaction between a fixed mass of Na2CO3 and 0.10 mol dm^-3 solutions of two acids X and Y. The curve for X rises more steeply than that for Y, but both curves level off at the same final volume of CO2. Which of the following statements about X and Y is false?
options: The rate of gas production is the same for X and Y.
The total volume of gas evolved is the same for X and Y.
X is a stronger acid than Y.
X ionizes more than Y in aqueous solution.
questions.explanation: The steeper curve for X shows a faster rate, so A is false; the same final level shows equal volumes.

questions.stem: The reaction represented by the equation below occurred in a sealed glass tube. N2O4(g) <=> 2NO2(g) (forward on heating, reverse on cooling); delta H = +x kJ mol^-1. What happens when the temperature is reduced at equilibrium?
options: The NO2 reacts with the N2O4.
The pressure exerted by the gases increases.
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic, so cooling favours the exothermic backward reaction and more N2O4 forms.

questions.stem: An oxidizing agent can be defined as
questions.explanation: An oxidizing agent removes hydrogen from (accepts hydrogen), adds oxygen to, or accepts electrons from another substance.

questions.stem: What are the values of x and y in the following equation? 2MnO4^- + xH^+ + yC2O4^2- -> 2Mn^2+ + 8H2O + 10CO2
questions.explanation: Carbon balance: 2y = 10, y = 5; hydrogen balance: x = 16 (8H2O).

questions.topic: Acids, bases and salts as electrolytes
questions.stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of electric current?
questions.explanation: Aqueous NaCl contains mobile Na^+ and Cl^- ions; the others are non-electrolytes.

questions.stem: Metal P will be above metal Q in the activity series if P
options: has a higher relative atomic mass than Q.
displaces ions of Q from solution.
is a better conductor of electricity than Q.
has a higher melting point than Q.
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from solutions of its ions.

questions.stem: Which of the following conversions involves electron gain?
questions.explanation: Cu^2+ + 2e^- -> Cu is a reduction (electron gain); the others are oxidations.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of boron in Na2B4O7?
Which of the following species undergoes oxidation during the electrolysis of dilute H2SO4?
questions.explanation: At the anode OH^- ions are discharged (oxidized): 4OH^- -> 2H2O + O2 + 4e^-.

questions.stem: C3H4 belongs to the same homologous series as
questions.explanation: C3H4 fits CnH2n-2 (alkynes); for n = 5 this is C5H8.

questions.stem: Alkanes can be prepared by
options: heating the sodium salt of an alkanoic acid with soda lime.
reacting a haloalkane with hot alcoholic KOH solution.
heating the ammonium salt of the corresponding alkanoic acid.
questions.explanation: Decarboxylation of sodium alkanoates with soda lime gives alkanes (e.g. CH3COONa gives CH4); B and C give alkenes.

questions.topic: Determination of formulae and structures of organic compounds
questions.stem: The empirical formula of a compound is C5H7N. If its relative molecular mass is 162, what is its molecular formula? [H = 1, C = 12, N = 14]
questions.explanation: Empirical mass = 60 + 7 + 14 = 81; n = 162/81 = 2, so the formula is C10H14N2.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds reacts readily with sodium to liberate hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Alkanols (here propan-2-ol) react with sodium to give the alkoxide and hydrogen.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of the compound with the structure CH3-CH(CH3)-C≡C-H (a terminal triple bond, with a methyl branch on the carbon next to it)?
questions.explanation: The main chain has four carbons with the triple bond at C-1 and a methyl group on C-3: 3-methylbut-1-yne.

questions.stem: Vegetable oils are converted into margarine by
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is added across the C=C bonds of the oil (nickel catalyst) to give a solid fat.

questions.stem: Hydrocarbons which react with ammoniacal copper (I) chloride solution conform to the general molecular formula
questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes (e.g. ethyne) give a red precipitate of copper (I) acetylide; alkynes are CnH2n-2.

questions.topic: Alkanoates as derivatives of alkanoic acids
questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will react together to give CH3(CH2)2COOCH3?
questions.explanation: Methyl butanoate is the ester of butanoic acid (CH3CH2CH2COOH) and methanol (CH3OH).

questions.stem: C12H26 and C12H22O11 are both covalent. C12H22O11 is soluble in water while C12H26 is insoluble. This is because C12H22O11
options: forms hydrogen bonds with the solvent.
contains stronger van der Waals' forces.
questions.explanation: Sucrose has many -OH groups which hydrogen-bond with water molecules.

questions.stem: The tensile strength of natural rubber is increased by heating it with
questions.explanation: Vulcanization (heating with sulphur) cross-links the rubber chains.

questions.stem: How many moles of oxygen are required to burn one mole of C4H8 completely?
Which of the following solutions react without producing a precipitate?
questions.explanation: The others give BaSO4, AgCl and Cu(OH)2 precipitates; HCl and KNO3 give only soluble products.

questions.stem: The use of silver salts in photography is based on the process of
options: oxidation of silver to silver halide.
reduction of silver ions to silver.
double decomposition to form silver halide.
direct combination of silver with halogens.
questions.explanation: Light reduces Ag^+ in silver halide to metallic silver, forming the image.

questions.stem: A sample of local gin that turned brown through storage in a rusty metal drum can be purified by
questions.explanation: Distillation separates the volatile gin from the dissolved/suspended rust colouring.

questions.stem: In the extraction of iron in the blast furnace, the role of limestone is to
options: oxidize red hot coke to carbon (IV) oxide.
questions.explanation: CaCO3 decomposes to CaO, which combines with SiO2 to form calcium silicate slag.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is most suitable for preventing the rusting of petroleum pipelines?
questions.explanation: Buried pipelines are protected sacrificially by connecting them to the more reactive magnesium.

questions.stem: Soldering wire is an alloy of tin and
questions.explanation: Solder is an alloy of tin and lead.

questions.stem: Which of the following pollutants is associated with genetic mutation?
questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation from radioactive fallout damages DNA and causes mutations.

questions.stem: Effects of water pollution include the following except
questions.explanation: Pollution adds (does not deplete) heavy metal ions.

questions.topic: Elements of the first transition series
questions.stem: (a)(i) List three characteristic properties of transition metals. (ii) Which of the following metals belong(s) to the first transition series? Chromium, Lead, Iron, Magnesium, Aluminium, Manganese. [6 marks] (b) Copy and complete the following table (columns: Alloy, Constituent elements, One major use) for: Bronze; Steel; Duralumin. [7 marks] (c) A razor blade of mass 5.00 g required 50.0 cm^3 of 2.00 mol dm^-3 HCl to react completely according to the equation below: Fe(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> FeCl2(aq) + H2(g). (i) Calculate the mass of iron in the blade. [Fe = 56.0] (ii) State two ways by which the reaction time can be reduced, assuming the blade retains its form at the start of the reaction. [7 marks] (d) A solid sample of a sodium salt X does not conduct electric current. (i) Give the reason for this observation. (ii) Suggest two ways by which X can be made to conduct. (iii) If X gave a greenish-yellow gas Y on warming with MnO2 and concentrated H2SO4, identify X and Y. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Any three: variable oxidation states; coloured compounds/ions; catalytic activity; formation of complex ions; paramagnetism; high melting points and densities (1 mark each)
3 marks: (a)(ii) Chromium, iron and manganese (1 mark each)
2 marks: (b) Bronze: copper and tin; use - statues/medals/bells/bearings
3 marks: (b) Steel: iron and carbon (plus e.g. Cr/Ni/Mn); use - construction, machinery, cutlery
2 marks: (b) Duralumin: aluminium, copper (with Mg, Mn); use - aircraft bodies/frames
1 mark: (c)(i) Moles of HCl = 50.0/1000 x 2.00 = 0.100 mol
1 mark: Moles of Fe = 0.100/2 = 0.0500 mol
2 marks: Mass of iron = 0.0500 x 56.0 = 2.80 g
3 marks: (c)(ii) Any two: warm the acid (raise temperature); use more concentrated acid; stir/agitate; add a catalyst (e.g. a few drops of CuSO4) (1.5 marks each)
1 mark: (d)(i) In the solid the ions are held in a rigid lattice and are not free to move
2 marks: (d)(ii) Melting (fusing) it; dissolving it in water
2 marks: (d)(iii) X is sodium chloride (NaCl); Y is chlorine (Cl2)
questions.explanation: (a) Transition metals show variable oxidation states, form coloured compounds and complex ions, and act as catalysts. Of the list, Cr, Fe and Mn are first-series transition metals. (b) Bronze = Cu + Sn (statues, medals); steel = Fe + C (construction, tools); duralumin = Al + Cu + Mg (aircraft). (c) n(HCl) = 0.100 mol, so n(Fe) = 0.0500 mol and mass = 2.80 g. The reaction is speeded up by heating, using more concentrated acid, stirring or adding a catalyst. (d) Ions in solid X are fixed in the lattice; X conducts when molten or in aqueous solution. Since warming with MnO2 and conc. H2SO4 gives greenish-yellow chlorine, X is NaCl and Y is Cl2.

questions.stem: (a)(i) Explain what is meant by ionization energy and state how it varies across a period in the Periodic Table. (ii) If the electronic configuration of an ion Q^2+ is 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6, give the: I. atomic number of Q. II. formula of the chloride of Q. III. reason why Q is described as an s-block element. [6 marks] (b)(i) Explain why isotopes have different mass numbers but are chemically alike. (ii) Calculate the relative atomic mass of an element R given that the relative abundance of 63/29 R and 65/29 R are 68% and 32% respectively. [5 marks] (c)(i) List two uses of chlorine. (ii) Give the balanced half equations for the following reaction: Cl2(g) + 2Br^-(aq) -> 2Cl^-(aq) + Br2(g). (iii) Given the following substances: CCl4(l), CuCl2(s), HCl(g), KCl(aq), state which of them I. has the highest entropy value; II. contain(s) chloride ions; III. can be decomposed by an electric current. [8 marks] (d) Consider the following equation: H2S(g) + M^2+(aq) <=> MS(s) + 2H^+(aq); delta H = -x kJ mol^-1. State and explain the effect of each of the following on the equilibrium position: (i) Increase in temperature; (ii) Addition of solution of M(NO3)2; (iii) Addition of acidified KMnO4(aq). [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron (the most loosely held) from a gaseous atom (1 mole of gaseous atoms) to form a positive ion
1 mark: It generally increases across a period (from left to right)
1 mark: (a)(ii) I. Atomic number of Q = 12
1 mark: II. QCl2
1 mark: III. Its outermost (valence) electrons are in an s orbital (3s^2)
2 marks: (b)(i) Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, so different mass numbers; they have the same number and arrangement of electrons (same electronic configuration), which determines chemical properties
1 mark: (b)(ii) RAM = (63 x 68 + 65 x 32)/100
2 marks: = 63.64 (63.6)
2 marks: (c)(i) Any two: water treatment/sterilisation; bleaching; manufacture of HCl, PVC, solvents, insecticides, disinfectants
1 mark: (c)(ii) Cl2 + 2e^- -> 2Cl^-
1 mark: 2Br^- -> Br2 + 2e^-
1 mark: (c)(iii) I. HCl(g)
2 marks: II. CuCl2(s) and KCl(aq)
1 mark: III. KCl(aq) (an electrolyte with mobile ions)
2 marks: (d)(i) Equilibrium shifts to the left, because the forward reaction is exothermic and a rise in temperature favours the endothermic (backward) reaction
2 marks: (d)(ii) Equilibrium shifts to the right, because the concentration of M^2+ (a reactant) is increased
2 marks: (d)(iii) Equilibrium shifts to the left, because KMnO4 oxidizes (removes) H2S, a reactant
questions.explanation: (a) Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove the most loosely bound electron from a gaseous atom; it increases across a period because nuclear charge increases while atomic radius decreases. Q^2+ has 10 electrons, so Q has Z = 12 (magnesium), its chloride is QCl2, and it is s-block because its outermost electrons (3s^2) are in an s orbital. (b) Isotopes differ in neutron number (so mass number) but have identical electronic configurations, hence identical chemistry. RAM = 0.68 x 63 + 0.32 x 65 = 63.64. (c) Chlorine is used for water treatment and bleaching. Half equations: Cl2 + 2e^- -> 2Cl^-; 2Br^- -> Br2 + 2e^-. HCl(g) has the highest entropy; CuCl2(s) and KCl(aq) contain chloride ions; KCl(aq) can be electrolysed. (d) Raising temperature shifts the exothermic equilibrium left; adding M(NO3)2 shifts it right; acidified KMnO4 oxidizes H2S, removing a reactant, so it shifts left.

questions.stem: (a) Write the name and structural formula of one compound conforming to each of the following: (i) CnH2n+2 (ii) CnH2n+1COOH (iii) CnH2n+1CHO [6 marks] (b)(i) Give one test for unsaturation. (ii) Consider the compound CH3-CH2-C≡C-CH3. I. Write its IUPAC name. II. State the product of its complete hydrogenation. III. Why does it not give a precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO3 whereas some homologues do? [6 marks] (c)(i) Write an equation for the reaction between propanol and sodium. (ii) State the reaction conditions for the conversion of ethanol to ethylpropanoate. (iii) Mention one reagent that can convert an alkanol to alkanoic acid. [6 marks] (d) The equation below represents one of the reactions of alkanes: C17H36(l) -> 3C2H4(g) + C8H18(l) + X. (i) Determine the formula of X and the homologous series to which it belongs. (ii) What type of reaction does the equation represent? (iii) Calculate the volume of ethene at s.t.p. that would be obtained from 0.100 mole of C17H36 in the reaction. [1 mole of a gas occupies 22.4 dm^3 at s.t.p.] [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) e.g. ethane, CH3-CH3 (name 1, structure 1)
2 marks: (a)(ii) e.g. ethanoic acid, CH3COOH (name 1, structure 1)
2 marks: (a)(iii) e.g. ethanal, CH3CHO (name 1, structure 1)
2 marks: (b)(i) Decolorises bromine water (or acidified/alkaline KMnO4) rapidly
1 mark: (b)(ii) I. Pent-2-yne
1 mark: II. Pentane (C5H12)
2 marks: III. It has no hydrogen atom on a triple-bonded carbon (not a terminal alkyne); only terminal alkynes with acidic H on C≡C form silver acetylides
2 marks: (c)(i) 2CH3CH2CH2OH + 2Na -> 2CH3CH2CH2ONa + H2
2 marks: (c)(ii) Heat (reflux) ethanol with propanoic acid in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 (catalyst)
2 marks: (c)(iii) Acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate (VI) (or acidified KMnO4)
1 mark: (d)(i) X = C3H6
1 mark: X is an alkene (propene)
1 mark: (d)(ii) Cracking
1 mark: (d)(iii) 1 mol C17H36 gives 3 mol C2H4, so 0.100 mol gives 0.300 mol
1 mark: Volume = 0.300 x 22.4
2 marks: = 6.72 dm^3
questions.explanation: (a) Ethane CH3CH3; ethanoic acid CH3COOH; ethanal CH3CHO. (b) Unsaturated compounds decolorise bromine water. CH3CH2C≡CCH3 is pent-2-yne; complete hydrogenation gives pentane; it does not react with ammoniacal AgNO3 because it has no acidic hydrogen on a triply bonded carbon. (c) 2C3H7OH + 2Na -> 2C3H7ONa + H2. Ethanol is refluxed with propanoic acid with concentrated H2SO4 as catalyst. Acidified K2Cr2O7 oxidizes alkanols to alkanoic acids. (d) Balancing C (17 - 6 - 8 = 3) and H (36 - 12 - 18 = 6) gives X = C3H6, an alkene; the reaction is cracking. 0.100 mol C17H36 gives 0.300 mol ethene = 6.72 dm^3 at s.t.p.

questions.stem: (a)(i) List three characteristic properties of acids. (ii) Given 0.10 mol dm^-3 solutions of HCl and CH3COOH, state and explain which of the acid solutions will have the higher electrical conductivity. (iii) Write one equation in each case to illustrate the behaviour of HNO3 as: I. a typical acid; II. an oxidizing agent. [10 marks] (b)(i) Draw and label a diagram for the laboratory preparation of sulphur (IV) oxide. (ii) Mention the catalyst used for the following reaction and explain its effect on the system: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g). [9 marks] (c) In the extraction of aluminium from bauxite, state the (i) substance used for digesting the ore; (ii) composition of the mixture electrolysed; (iii) anode material and give the reason why it has to be changed at intervals. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Any three: sour taste; turn blue litmus red; react with bases to form salt and water; liberate CO2 from trioxocarbonates (IV); react with active metals to give hydrogen; pH below 7
1 mark: (a)(ii) HCl
2 marks: HCl is a strong acid that ionizes completely, so it contains more ions (H3O^+, Cl^-) than CH3COOH, a weak acid that is only partially ionized
2 marks: (a)(iii) I. e.g. HNO3 + NaOH -> NaNO3 + H2O (or with CaCO3/CuO)
2 marks: II. e.g. Cu + 4HNO3(conc) -> Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O (or 3Cu + 8HNO3 -> 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O; or C/S oxidation)
2 marks: (b)(i) Reactants: sodium sulphite (Na2SO3) and dilute HCl (or Cu and conc. H2SO4 with heat)
2 marks: Apparatus: flask with thistle/dropping funnel, delivery tube; gas dried through concentrated H2SO4
2 marks: Collection by downward delivery (upward displacement of air), as SO2 is denser than air; correct labels
1 mark: (b)(ii) Vanadium (V) oxide (V2O5) (or platinum)
2 marks: It increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached (lowers activation energy) but does not alter the position of equilibrium/yield
2 marks: (c)(i) Sodium hydroxide solution (concentrated NaOH)
2 marks: (c)(ii) Purified aluminium oxide (alumina) dissolved in molten cryolite (Na3AlF6)
1 mark: (c)(iii) Anode: carbon (graphite)
1 mark: The oxygen liberated at the anode burns (oxidizes) the carbon to CO2, so the anode wears away
questions.explanation: (a) Acids taste sour, turn blue litmus red and react with bases to form salt and water (also liberate CO2 from carbonates). 0.10 mol dm^-3 HCl conducts better because it is a strong acid, fully ionized, while ethanoic acid is only partly ionized. As an acid: HNO3 + NaOH -> NaNO3 + H2O; as an oxidizing agent: Cu + 4HNO3 -> Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O. (b) SO2 is made by adding dilute HCl to sodium sulphite in a flask fitted with a funnel, drying through conc. H2SO4 and collecting by downward delivery. The catalyst V2O5 speeds up attainment of equilibrium without shifting it. (c) Bauxite is digested with NaOH; the electrolyte is pure alumina dissolved in molten cryolite; the carbon anodes are burnt away by the oxygen evolved and must be replaced periodically.

questions.stem: (a) What is meant by each of the following terms? (i) Enthalpy of combustion (ii) Structural isomers [4 marks] (b)(i) What type of oxide is each of the following? NO2, CO, Fe2O3, Al2O3, P2O3 (ii) Mention one oxide associated with global warming. [6 marks] (c)(i) State the main processes involved in the industrial production of oxygen from air. (ii) Write equations to show the action of heat on each of KNO3 and NaHCO3. (iii) Calculate the number of molecules in 4.00 g of oxygen. [O = 16.0; Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23 mol^-1] [9 marks] (d)(i) List two metals that can displace iron (II) ions from solution. (ii) During the extraction of iron in the blast furnace, oxygen combines with one of the raw materials to form a reducing agent W. Identify W and the raw material that produces it. (iii) What property is exhibited in each case when the following changes occur on exposure? I. Fe(s) converted to Fe2O3.xH2O II. FeCl3(s) converted to FeCl3(aq) [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) The heat evolved when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in oxygen (under standard conditions)
2 marks: (a)(ii) Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (arrangements of atoms)
1 mark: (b)(i) NO2 - acidic (mixed anhydride)
1 mark: CO - neutral
1 mark: Fe2O3 - basic
1 mark: Al2O3 - amphoteric
1 mark: P2O3 - acidic
1 mark: (b)(ii) Carbon (IV) oxide (CO2) (or nitrogen (I) oxide)
1 mark: (c)(i) Air is purified (dust, CO2 and water vapour removed)
1 mark: then liquefied by repeated compression and cooling (expansion)
1 mark: and the liquid air is fractionally distilled; nitrogen (b.p. -196 C) boils off first, leaving oxygen (b.p. -183 C)
2 marks: (c)(ii) 2KNO3 -> 2KNO2 + O2
2 marks: 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2
1 mark: (c)(iii) Moles of O2 = 4.00/32.0 = 0.125 mol
1 mark: Number of molecules = 0.125 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 7.53 x 10^22
2 marks: (d)(i) Any two metals above iron, e.g. zinc, magnesium, aluminium
2 marks: (d)(ii) W is carbon (II) oxide (CO); produced from coke
1 mark: (d)(iii) I. Corrosion (rusting)
1 mark: II. Deliquescence
questions.explanation: (a) Enthalpy of combustion is the heat evolved when one mole of a substance burns completely in oxygen; structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures. (b) NO2 acidic, CO neutral, Fe2O3 basic, Al2O3 amphoteric, P2O3 acidic; CO2 causes global warming. (c) Oxygen is obtained by fractional distillation of purified, liquefied air. 2KNO3 -> 2KNO2 + O2; 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2. 4.00 g O2 = 0.125 mol = 7.53 x 10^22 molecules. (d) Zn and Mg displace Fe^2+. W is CO, formed when coke burns in limited oxygen. Iron rusts (corrosion) and FeCl3 absorbs moisture and dissolves (deliquescence).

questions.stem: (a)(i) State Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes. (ii) The following reaction occurred when 100 cm^3 of carbon (II) oxide was burnt in 70 cm^3 of oxygen: 2CO(g) + O2(g) -> 2CO2(g). Calculate the total volume of gas mixture in the reaction vessel at the end of the reaction, assuming the temperature and pressure were adjusted to the initial values. [6 marks] (b)(i) List two uses of H2SO4. (ii) Give equations and reaction conditions for the following conversions: ZnCO3(s) -> ZnO(s) -> ZnSO4(aq). (iii) State how each of the following can be obtained from ZnSO4(aq). I. ZnSO4(s) II. ZnCO3(s) [10 marks] (c) Give the reason for each of the following: (i) Graphite is soft while diamond, its allotrope, is hard. (ii) Sodium salts cannot be prepared by double decomposition. (iii) Na2CO3(aq) which is a salt solution, turns red litmus blue. [6 marks] (d)(i) Mention two types of coal. (ii) Name the process by which benzene is obtained from coal tar. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) When gases react, they do so in volumes which bear a simple ratio to one another and to the volumes of the products, if gaseous, at the same temperature and pressure
1 mark: (a)(ii) 100 cm^3 CO reacts with 50 cm^3 O2
1 mark: 100 cm^3 CO2 formed
1 mark: Unreacted O2 = 70 - 50 = 20 cm^3
1 mark: Total volume = 100 + 20 = 120 cm^3
2 marks: (b)(i) Any two: manufacture of fertilizers (ammonium sulphate, superphosphate); car battery electrolyte; drying agent; manufacture of detergents, paints, dyes; refining petroleum
2 marks: (b)(ii) ZnCO3 -> ZnO + CO2
1 mark: Condition: heat (strongly)
2 marks: ZnO + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2O
1 mark: Condition: dilute H2SO4, warm (add oxide until in excess and filter)
1 mark: (b)(iii) I. Evaporate the solution to concentrate it and allow to crystallize (crystallization)
1 mark: II. Add sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) solution; filter, wash and dry the ZnCO3 precipitate
2 marks: (c)(i) Graphite has a layer structure with weak van der Waals forces between layers, so layers slide; diamond has a rigid 3-D tetrahedral network of strong covalent bonds
2 marks: (c)(ii) All sodium salts are soluble in water, so no precipitate forms
2 marks: (c)(iii) Na2CO3 is a salt of a strong base and weak acid; it hydrolyses in water to produce excess OH^- ions, so the solution is alkaline
2 marks: (d)(i) Any two: peat, lignite, bituminous coal, anthracite
1 mark: (d)(ii) Fractional distillation
questions.explanation: (a) Gay-Lussac: reacting gases and gaseous products are in simple whole-number volume ratios at constant temperature and pressure. 100 cm^3 CO uses 50 cm^3 O2 to give 100 cm^3 CO2, leaving 20 cm^3 O2: total 120 cm^3. (b) H2SO4 is used for fertilizers and in lead-acid batteries. Heat ZnCO3 -> ZnO + CO2; ZnO + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2O. Crystallize ZnSO4 by evaporation; precipitate ZnCO3 by adding Na2CO3 solution. (c) Graphite's layers held by weak forces slide over each other; diamond is a rigid covalent network. Sodium salts are all soluble so cannot be precipitated. Na2CO3 hydrolyses to give OH^- ions. (d) Peat, lignite, bituminous coal, anthracite; benzene is obtained by fractional distillation of coal tar.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is monoatomic?
questions.explanation: Mg^2+ consists of a single atom; the others are polyatomic ions.

questions.stem: The correct electron configuration of an element 20W is
questions.explanation: Filling in order of increasing energy: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 (20 electrons).

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of elements has the same outermost electron configuration? I. H, He, Be. II. H, Li, Be. III. H, Li, Na. IV. He, Ne, Ar.

questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases steadily down a group as atomic size increases; atomic and ionic radii increase, and electron affinity does not fall regularly (e.g. Cl is higher than F).

options: the presence of electrostatic forces of attraction.
their ability to dissolve in water.
their ability to exist as solids.
their ability to conduct electricity in the molten state.

questions.explanation: N2 has a triple bond (N≡N), the strongest of these.

questions.explanation: Water is V-shaped (bent) because of the two lone pairs on oxygen; the others are linear.

options: absence of attractive forces between molecules.
collisions between the molecules and the walls of the container.

options: small number of molecules escaping into gaseous state.
large number of molecules escaping into gaseous state.

there is no loss of energy during collision.
they move randomly in straight lines.

By-products are slag (CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3) and furnace gases (e.g. CO from CO2 + C -> 2CO). (c) Steel: Fe, C; bronze: Cu, Sn; brass: Cu, Zn; soft solder: Pb, Sn. questions.stem: (a)(i) What is the shape of I. s-orbital; II. p-orbital? (ii) Which ion has the following composition? 0 - electron, 2 - protons and 2 - neutrons. [3 marks] (b) The following table shows the melting and boiling points of oxides of the elements X, Y and Z: X2O - melting point 1403 K, boiling point 2223 K; Y2O - melting point 273 K, boiling point 373 K; Z2O - melting point 49 K, boiling point 128 K. Z2O respectively? [8 marks] (c) The following equation illustrates homogeneous equilibrium established when hydrogen and carbon (IV) oxide react: H2(g) + CO2(g) <=> H2O(g) + CO(g). (i) Why is this reaction regarded as homogeneous? (ii) Explain briefly the effect of an increase in pressure on the: I. equilibrium position; II. reaction rate. (iii) State three features of an equilibrium reaction. [8 marks] (d) A compound Q contains 29.1% sodium, 40.5% sulphur and 30.4% oxygen. Determine the: (i) empirical formula; (ii) molecular formula of Q if its relative molar mass is 158. [O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, S = 32.0] [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) I. s-orbital is spherical
1 mark: II. p-orbital is dumb-bell shaped
1 mark: (a)(ii) The helium ion He^2+ (alpha particle)
1 mark: (b)(i) X - ionic (electrovalent)
1 mark: Y - covalent
1 mark: Z - covalent
2 marks: (b)(ii) Each Z atom shares one pair of electrons with the oxygen atom (two shared pairs), so each atom attains a stable octet/duplet configuration
2 marks: (b)(iii) I. Y2O: hydrogen bonds (Y2O is water)
1 mark: II. Z2O: van der Waals' (dispersion/dipole) forces
1 mark: (c)(i) All the reactants and products are in the same phase (gaseous)
2 marks: (c)(ii) I. No effect on the equilibrium position, since there are equal numbers of moles (volumes) of gas on both sides (2 = 2)
2 marks: II. Rate increases, because the gases are more concentrated and collide more frequently (both forward and backward rates increase)
3 marks: (c)(iii) Any three: it is dynamic (forward rate = backward rate); concentrations of reactants and products remain constant; it is attained only in a closed system; it can be approached from either direction; macroscopic properties are constant
1 mark: (d)(i) Na: 29.1/23.0 = 1.265; S: 40.5/32.0 = 1.266; O: 30.4/16.0 = 1.90
1 mark: Dividing by the smallest: 1 : 1 : 1.5
2 marks: Empirical formula = Na2S2O3
1 mark: (d)(ii) (Na2S2O3)n = 158; empirical formula mass = 46 + 64 + 48 = 158, so n = 1
1 mark: Molecular formula = Na2S2O3
questions.explanation: (a) s-orbitals are spherical, p-orbitals dumb-bell shaped; 2 protons, 2 neutrons and no electrons is He^2+ (an alpha particle). (b) The very high melting point of X2O shows ionic bonding; Y2O and Z2O are covalent. In Z2O each Z atom shares a pair of electrons with oxygen. Y2O (m.p. 273 K, b.p. 373 K - water) is held by hydrogen bonds; Z2O by weak van der Waals' forces. (c) All species are gases, hence homogeneous. Raising pressure has no effect on position because gaseous moles are equal on both sides, but it increases the rate by increasing concentration. Equilibrium is dynamic, has constant concentrations, and requires a closed system. (d) Mole ratio Na : S : O = 1.265 : 1.266 : 1.90 = 2 : 2 : 3, so the empirical formula is Na2S2O3 (mass 158), which is also the molecular formula.

questions.stem: (a)(i) What is meant by saponification? (ii) List the raw materials needed for the manufacture of soap. (iii) Name the main by-product obtained from the manufacture of soap. [5 marks] (b) What type of reaction is represented by each of the following equations? (i) C3H8 + Cl2 -> C3H7Cl + HCl (ii) n(CH2=CH2) -> -(CH2-CH2)n- (iii) C16H34 -> 3C2H4 + C10H22 (iv) C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6 (v) C2H5OH + H2SO4 -> C2H5HSO4 + H2O [5 marks] (c) An organic compound U produces effervescence when reacted with sodium metal liberating gas V. (i) Write the functional group present in U and W. (ii) Identify gases V and G. (iii) Name the type of reaction between: I. U and sodium metal; II. U and W. (iv) Name the catalyst used in the reaction between U and W. (v) If the molar mass of W is 74 g mol^-1, deduce the: I. molecular formula; II. structural formula of the compound. [H = 1.00; C = 12.0; O = 16.0] [12 marks] (d) Explain briefly why the reaction between magnesium and 1.0 mol dm^-3 ethanoic acid would be slower than the reaction between magnesium and 1.0 mol dm^-3 hydrochloric acid. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils (esters) by boiling with caustic alkali (NaOH/KOH) to form soap and glycerol
2 marks: (a)(ii) Fats or oils (e.g. palm oil); sodium or potassium hydroxide; (sodium chloride for salting out)
1 mark: (a)(iii) Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol)
1 mark: (b)(i) Substitution
1 mark: (ii) (Addition) polymerization
1 mark: (iii) Cracking
1 mark: (iv) Addition (hydrogenation)
1 mark: (v) Esterification (or neutralization/substitution forming ethyl hydrogensulphate)
2 marks: (c)(i) U: hydroxyl group, -OH (alkanol); W: carboxyl group, -COOH (alkanoic acid)
2 marks: (c)(ii) V is hydrogen; G is carbon (IV) oxide
1 mark: (c)(iii) I. Displacement (substitution/redox)
1 mark: II. Esterification
1 mark: (c)(iv) Concentrated tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
1 mark: (c)(v) CnH2n+1COOH: 14n + 46 = 74, so n = 2
2 marks: I. Molecular formula C3H6O2 (C2H5COOH)
2 marks: II. CH3-CH2-COOH (propanoic acid)
2 marks: (d) Ethanoic acid is a weak acid and is only partially ionized, so its solution contains a lower concentration of H^+ (H3O^+) ions than HCl, which is fully ionized
1 mark: Fewer H^+ ions collide with the magnesium per unit time, so the rate is slower
questions.explanation: (a) Saponification is the hydrolysis of fats or oils by caustic alkali to give soap and glycerol; raw materials are fats/oils and NaOH or KOH (with brine); the by-product is glycerol. (b) Substitution; polymerization; cracking; addition (hydrogenation); esterification. (c) U is an alkanol (-OH) and W an alkanoic acid (-COOH); V is H2 and G is CO2; U + Na is a displacement (redox) reaction and U + W is esterification catalysed by concentrated H2SO4. W, CnH2n+1COOH with M = 74, gives n = 2: C2H5COOH, i.e. CH3CH2COOH. (d) Ethanoic acid is weak and only partly ionized, so [H^+] is much lower than in 1.0 mol dm^-3 HCl and magnesium reacts more slowly.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] (a)(i) Define hybridization. (ii) Explain briefly how sp^3 hybrid orbitals are formed. [5 marks] (b) Consider the equilibrium reaction represented by the following equation: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) -> 2SO3(g); delta H = -x kJ mol^-1. (i) Write an expression for the equilibrium constant Kp. (ii) Sketch the energy profile diagram for the forward reaction indicating the position of I. reactants and products; II. activated complex; III. enthalpy change; IV. activation energy. [7 marks] (c)(i) Calculate the pH of a solution containing 4.0 x 10^-5 mol dm^-3 hydrogen ion. (ii) Indicate whether the solution is acidic or basic. Give a reason for your answer. [5 marks] (d) Give three differences between the solubilities of solids in liquids and gases in liquids. [3 marks] (e) Calculate the volume occupied by 0.125 moles of oxygen at 27 degrees C and pressure of 2.02 x 10^5 Nm^-2. [standard pressure = 1.01 x 10^5 Nm^-2; 1 mole of gas occupies 22.4 dm^3 at s.t.p.] [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Hybridization is the mixing of atomic orbitals of similar energy in an atom to form an equal number of new, equivalent (hybrid) orbitals
3 marks: (a)(ii) e.g. in carbon, one 2s electron is promoted to the empty 2p orbital; the one 2s and three 2p orbitals then mix to give four equivalent sp^3 orbitals directed tetrahedrally (109.5 degrees)
3 marks: (b)(i) Kp = (pSO3)^2 / [(pSO2)^2 x pO2]
1 mark: (b)(ii) I. Reactants (2SO2 + O2) at a higher energy level than products (2SO3)
1 mark: II. Activated complex at the peak of the curve
1 mark: III. Enthalpy change shown as the (negative) drop from reactants to products
1 mark: IV. Activation energy shown from reactants up to the peak
1 mark: (c)(i) pH = -log[H^+] = -log(4.0 x 10^-5)
2 marks: pH = 4.4
2 marks: (c)(ii) Acidic, because the pH is less than 7
1 mark: (d) Solubility of most solids increases with temperature, while that of gases decreases
1 mark: Pressure has little effect on solubility of solids but solubility of gases increases with pressure (Henry's law)
1 mark: Dissolved solids are recovered by evaporation/crystallization; dissolved gases are expelled by boiling/heating
1 mark: (e) T1 = 273 K, P1 = 1.01 x 10^5 Nm^-2, V1 = 0.125 x 22.4 = 2.80 dm^3
1 mark: T2 = 300 K, P2 = 2.02 x 10^5 Nm^-2
1 mark: V2 = P1V1T2/(T1P2)
2 marks: V2 = (1.01 x 10^5 x 2.80 x 300)/(273 x 2.02 x 10^5) = 1.54 dm^3
questions.explanation: (a) Hybridization is the mixing of atomic orbitals of comparable energy to form equivalent hybrid orbitals; in carbon a 2s electron is promoted and the 2s and three 2p orbitals combine into four tetrahedral sp^3 orbitals. (b) Kp = p(SO3)^2/(p(SO2)^2 x p(O2)). The profile rises from reactants to a peak (activated complex) and falls to products at a lower level; the rise is the activation energy and the overall drop is delta H (negative). (c) pH = -log(4.0 x 10^-5) = 4.4, acidic since below 7. (d) Solid solubility usually rises with temperature but gas solubility falls; pressure strongly affects gases but not solids; solids are recovered by evaporation, gases are driven off by heating. (e) V at s.t.p. = 2.80 dm^3; V = 2.80 x (1.01/2.02) x (300/273) = 1.54 dm^3.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Nigeria, Sierra Leone and The Gambia] (a)(i) Distinguish between a primary cell and a secondary cell. (ii) Give one example of each cell in 7(a)(i). [4 marks] (b) In a cell set-up, a copper metal rod dips into CuSO4(aq) in one beaker and a silver metal rod dips into AgNO3(aq) in another beaker. The two metals are connected by a wire through an instrument X, and the two solutions are connected by Y. The standard electrode potentials for copper and silver are: E(Cu^2+/Cu) = +0.34 V; E(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80 V. (i) Name the reference against which other electrode potentials are measured. (ii) Which instrument should be at position X? (iii) What is Y? State its function. (iv) Calculate the e.m.f. of the cell. [7 marks] (c) Explain briefly why electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium chloride does not produce sodium at the cathode. [3 marks] (d)(i) What is meant by nuclear fission? (ii) How could electrical energy be generated by nuclear fission? [5 marks] (e) Turpentine was burnt in chlorine gas resulting in the formation of the products as illustrated below: C10H16(l) + 8Cl2(g) -> 10C(s) + 16HCl(g). Calculate the mass of turpentine that would completely burn in 21.3 g of chlorine. [H = 1.00; C = 12.0; Cl = 35.5] [6 marks]

2 marks: (a)(i) A primary cell cannot be recharged (its chemical reaction is irreversible); a secondary cell can be recharged by passing current through it (reversible reaction)
2 marks: (a)(ii) Primary: Leclanche (dry) cell or Daniell cell; secondary: lead-acid accumulator or nickel-iron (alkaline) cell
1 mark: (b)(i) Standard hydrogen electrode
1 mark: (b)(ii) Voltmeter (high-resistance voltmeter/potentiometer)
1 mark: (b)(iii) Y is a salt bridge
2 marks: It completes the circuit by allowing ions to move between the two half-cells and maintains electrical neutrality, without mixing the solutions
1 mark: (b)(iv) E(cell) = E(cathode) - E(anode) = 0.80 - 0.34

3 marks: (c) H^+ ions (from water) are lower than Na^+ in the electrochemical series and are preferentially discharged at the cathode, so hydrogen is liberated instead of sodium (any sodium formed would react with water)
2 marks: (d)(i) Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. U-235) into two lighter nuclei of similar mass, by bombardment with neutrons, with release of a large amount of energy and more neutrons
3 marks: (d)(ii) The heat released in a controlled chain reaction in a nuclear reactor is used to boil water into steam, which drives turbines connected to generators to produce electricity

questions.explanation: (a) A primary cell cannot be recharged (e.g. Leclanche dry cell); a secondary cell can be recharged (e.g. lead-acid accumulator). (b) Potentials are measured against the standard hydrogen electrode; X is a voltmeter; Y is a salt bridge, which completes the circuit and maintains neutrality by allowing ion migration; e.m.f. = 0.80 - 0.34 = 0.46 V. (c) H^+ is preferentially discharged because it is lower in the electrochemical series than Na^+, so hydrogen is evolved. (d) Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus by neutrons into lighter nuclei with release of energy; in a reactor this heat produces steam to drive turbo-generators. (e) 21.3 g Cl2 = 0.300 mol, so 0.0375 mol C10H16 = 5.10 g.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Nigeria, Sierra Leone and The Gambia] (a) Describe briefly how each of the following aqueous solutions could be identified in the laboratory: (i) ammonium trioxocarbonate (IV); (ii) ammonium chloride. [6 marks] (b) Arrange the following compounds in order of increasing boiling point and give reasons for your answer: CS2, NaF and CO2. [5 marks] (c) List two gases each that are: (i) acidic; (ii) highly soluble in water; (iii) oxidized by acidified KMnO4(aq). [6 marks] (d) In a tabular form, compare the elements silicon and sulphur under the following properties: (i) metallic character; (ii) physical state; (iii) conduction of electricity. [3 marks] (e) A cuboid piece of sodium metal measures 3 cm x 4 cm x 10 cm. If the density of sodium is 0.971 g cm^-3, calculate the number of atoms in the sodium metal. [Na = 23; Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23 mol^-1] [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Warm a portion with NaOH(aq): a gas that turns damp red litmus blue (NH3) is evolved, showing NH4^+
2 marks: Add dilute acid (HCl) to another portion: effervescence of a gas that turns lime water milky (CO2), showing CO3^2-
1 mark: (a)(ii) Warm with NaOH(aq): ammonia evolved (turns damp red litmus blue), showing NH4^+
2 marks: Acidify with dilute HNO3 and add AgNO3(aq): white precipitate soluble in excess NH3(aq), showing Cl^-
2 marks: (b) Order: CO2 < CS2 < NaF
1 mark: CO2 and CS2 are simple covalent molecules held by weak van der Waals' forces
1 mark: CS2 has a larger molar mass (more electrons) than CO2, so stronger van der Waals' forces and a higher boiling point (CS2 is liquid, CO2 a gas)
1 mark: NaF is ionic with strong electrostatic forces in its lattice, so it has the highest boiling point
2 marks: (c)(i) Any two acidic gases: CO2, SO2, NO2, HCl, H2S
2 marks: (c)(ii) Any two highly soluble gases: NH3, HCl, SO2
2 marks: (c)(iii) Any two: SO2, H2S, ethene (C2H4) (or HCl conc.)
1 mark: (d)(i) Metallic character: silicon is a metalloid; sulphur is a non-metal
1 mark: (d)(ii) Physical state: both are solids at room temperature (Si - hard giant covalent solid; S - brittle yellow molecular solid)
1 mark: (d)(iii) Conduction: silicon is a semiconductor; sulphur is a non-conductor (insulator)
1 mark: (e) Volume = 3 x 4 x 10 = 120 cm^3
1 mark: Mass = 120 x 0.971 = 116.5 g
1 mark: Moles = 116.5/23 = 5.066 mol
2 marks: Number of atoms = 5.066 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 3.05 x 10^24
questions.explanation: (a) Both give ammonia (turns damp red litmus blue) when warmed with NaOH. Ammonium trioxocarbonate (IV) effervesces with dilute acid giving CO2 (turns lime water milky); ammonium chloride gives a white precipitate with acidified AgNO3. (b) CO2 < CS2 < NaF: CO2 and CS2 are molecular with weak van der Waals' forces, stronger in the heavier CS2; NaF is ionic with strong lattice forces. (c) Acidic: CO2, SO2; very soluble: NH3, HCl; oxidized by acidified KMnO4: SO2, H2S. (d) Si is a metalloid and semiconductor, S a non-metal and insulator; both are solids. (e) 120 cm^3 x 0.971 g/cm^3 = 116.5 g = 5.066 mol = 3.05 x 10^24 atoms.
